name: Hester Lake Route

pitch_detail.notes: Price Creek gully, ~3,200-3,800 ft — the most technical section of the approach per multiple trip reports.
Boulder field south of Little Hester Lake up the east ridge (near Pt. 5,480'/5,440'), traverse to the ~5,400 ft col, final ridge scramble to the 5,587 ft summit.

beta: From the Dingford Creek Trailhead, follow the Dingford Creek Trail (multiple creek crossings) toward Hester Lake and Little Hester Lake — roughly the first 5-6 miles. Leave the trail and make an ascending traverse below cliff bands, climbing a short, steep gully along Price Creek between about 3,200 and 3,800 ft — reported by multiple parties as the most technical part of the scramble. From the lakes basin, ascend the boulder field south of Little Hester Lake to gain Price's east ridge near Point 5,480'/5,440', traverse the steep north side of the ridge to a col around 5,400 ft just east of the true summit, and finish with a short ridge scramble to the 5,587 ft summit. Expect Class 3 scrambling with occasional steep snow or rock gullies on the ridge, and real routefinding difficulty — at least one party's own GPS track diverged noticeably between ascent and descent.
pro_tips: Carry a GPS track from a prior trip report if possible — at least one party's own GPS failed mid-climb and their documented ascent line proved suboptimal.
The Price Creek gully (3,200-3,800 ft) is the technical crux of the approach; scout it in good visibility before committing.
